attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: Unhedged 'will' chain: AI lets the AMPTP cut rooms to one person plus a machine, which shrinks WGA membership and eventually destroys the union. No deadline. The paraphrase keeps the chain.

contract.note: It requires the whole causal chain ending in destruction to support, and a decisive terminal event to contradict. That is a fair, ordinary reading of an 'eventually' forecast with no deadline.

evidence.note: 2023 WGA agreement bars companies from requiring writers to use AI. An obstacle to the mechanism, but not a terminal event.
WGA ratified a 2026–2030 agreement in April 2026, so the union is still bargaining. Survival for a finite period does not contradict an eventual forecast.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given, and no terminal event either way appears in the packet. The union was still bargaining in 2026 and the 2023 contract limits forced AI use, but neither rules out eventual destruction. The forecast stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: Firm 'will become increasingly rare' about AI-driven customer service, with no deadline. The context's 'not every company' scope limit is kept in the contract.

contract.note: Reading 'distance from responsibility' as reduced practical access to someone who can resolve problems is an ordinary reading. It requires a representative trend across adopting companies, not every firm.

evidence.note: Klarna's own 2024 disclosure that AI handles two-thirds of its chats. One company, self-reported, so it shows adoption but not a broad sustained trend.
Klarna kept a live-agent option. One company's design choice, not representative evidence against the trend.
CFPB 2023 report of chatbot 'doom loop' complaints. Consistent with the claim but anecdotal and not longitudinal.
CFPB says firms keep legal service obligations. Relevant only to a legal-liability reading, not to practical access.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given. The packet has one company's disclosures and complaint anecdotes, but no representative longitudinal data on the share of human interactions or on access to resolution. Neither the trend nor its consequence is settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: The sentence names AI alongside streaming as causes, so 'in part' is faithful. The share-value assertion is rightly left out. 'Assuming a great deal' admits inference, but 'very clearly' is firm.

contract.note: It fairly separates two parts: that AI was a material disputed issue, and the executive motive attributed to it. Both are needed for support.

evidence.note: WGA comparison table: the AMPTP rejected AI restrictions as of May 1, 2023. Supports the dispute part only. It comes from a party to the dispute.
AMPTP's own May 4 explanation that AI needs more discussion. A company statement, so it neither proves nor disproves the motive.
TIME, May 2023: AI was one aspect of the dispute. Corroborates the dispute part, not the motive.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows AI was a substantive point of dispute before the strike. Nothing in the packet independently shows that executives wanted to use AI to write content, or that this motive drove the strike. The AMPTP's alternative account does not disprove it either. The causal claim as framed stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: A present-tense statement about capability and its limits. 'Can mimic' states a capability, not a probability hedge.

contract.note: Reading empathy as felt concern and responsibility as the agent's own accountability is ordinary. The May 1–12 window is strict for an ongoing capability, since earlier demonstrations get demoted to context, but this is not unfair to the speaker.

evidence.note: Intercom's March 2023 description of Fin handling multi-turn support conversations. Plausibly shows mimicry, but it is the vendor's own claim and falls outside the window.
2021 preprint on chatbots displaying empathy. Behavioural only, so it says nothing about felt concern. Outside the period.

reviews.rationale: The capability evidence predates the target window and comes from a vendor. Nothing in the packet addresses felt empathy or the agent's own accountability, so the claim cannot be confirmed or refuted on this record.
